items.title: LFM2.5-24B-A2B: Built for fast on-device agents
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.liquid.ai/blog/lfm2-5-24b-a2b Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50097369 Points: 246 # Comments: 58
items.content:
Today, we release LFM2.5-24B-A2B , a 24B-parameter reasoning model with just 2B active parameters, built for fast, private agents on-device. It is the largest and final model in the LFM2.5 family, which now spans two orders of magnitude: from LFM2.5-230M to LFM2.5-24B-A2B .

LFM2.5-24B-A2B is competitive with Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, a model with ~50% more total and active parameters, on five of eight agentic and tool-use benchmarks, scoring 48.09 on LiveClaw versus 38.19 and 27.69 on AutomationBench versus 8.72. Because only 2B parameters are active per token, it runs up to 1.7× faster than comparable MoEs on-device, with 184 tokens/s on an Apple M5 Max and up to 21K output tokens/s on a single NVIDIA B300 GPU.

The base (LFM2.5-24B-A2B-Base) and post-trained (LFM2.5-24B-A2B) models are open-weight and available today on Hugging Face and our Playground . Check out our docs on how to run and fine-tune it locally.

LFM2.5-24B-A2B builds on our previous LFM2-24B-A2B release, with an expanded vocabulary and context window, scaled-up pretraining, and large-scale reinforcement learning. Unlike its predecessor, LFM2.5-24B-A2B is a reasoning-only model that produces an explicit chain of thought before its final answer. We adopted this strategy to leverage its high decode speed and improve answer quality.

Architecture. It keeps the 40 layers, 64 experts per MoE block with top-4 routing, and the same hybrid of gated short convolutions and GQA. The two architectural changes are the context window extension from 32,768 to 131,072 tokens, and the in-place tokenizer expansion , which doubles the vocabulary from 65K to 128K tokens for better non-Latin tokenization.

Mid-training has two phases. The first runs 2T tokens at 32K context on curated, higher-quality data weighted toward reasoning, math, code, instruction following, and multilingual text. The second runs 300B tokens at 131K context, weighted toward long context data. Tool calls and multi-turn trajectories appear throughout both phases to prepare the model for agentic workloads.

During teacher specialization, LFM2.5-24B-A2B exhibited well-known reward-hacking behaviors: searching for the final answer in a repository's git history or on platforms like GitHub, PyPI, and Hugging Face. More surprisingly, it even figured out it was in a sandbox, as shown in the examples below.

items.title: India and China aren't friends - but Nepal wants to unite them against climate threats
items.summary: Can Nepal bring the two regional giants together to confront a shared climate threat in the Himalayas?
items.content:
Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah used much of his speech at the recent UN General Assembly to warn of the growing threat of climate-related disasters in the Himalayas, recalling the devastating debris floods that struck his country in August.

But it was his ambitious proposal to bring together regional rivals India and China, alongside Nepal, to tackle these shared threats that drew particular attention.

Shah called for the creation of a Himalayan Climate Resilience Mechanism to strengthen cross-border disaster response and the sharing of scientific data and expertise in one of the world's most environmentally fragile and geopolitically sensitive regions.

"Let the Himalayas become a laboratory of international co-operation rather than a frontier of fragmented information," he said.

A senior official at Nepal's foreign ministry, speaking on condition of anonymity, said the proposal was still at an early stage.

"The PM's proposal has given a political direction. Our ministry is working with other relevant agencies to put forward a preliminary framework which can be the basis for building common understanding," the official said.

Neither India nor China has formally responded to the proposal. The BBC has contacted their foreign ministries for comment.

But can Nepal really bring the two regional giants together to confront a shared climate threat in a region where they have long been locked in bitter territorial disputes?

India and China share a disputed frontier stretching roughly 3,500km (2,175 miles), much of it across the Himalayas. Their competing territorial claims have led to a war, deadly clashes and repeated military stand-offs along the Line of Actual Control (LAC), the de facto boundary separating areas under their control.

But the mountains that have long been a source of friction between the two countries are also facing an urgent climate threat.

Temperatures in the Himalayan region are rising faster than the global average, accelerating glacier retreat and permafrost thaw and contributing to growing risks of landslides, rockfalls, avalanches and glacial lake outburst floods.

Such disasters can sweep across national boundaries, threatening lives, infrastructure and livelihoods far downstream - making co-operation between the countries sharing the Himalayas increasingly important.

A report by the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development , external released in March found that glaciers across the Hindu Kush Himalaya (HKH) region are melting at an accelerating pace, with the rate of ice loss having doubled since 2000 compared with the 1974-1999 period.

Further east, on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, glaciers have shrunk by 24% in area over the past six decades, Kang Shichang, director of the Chinese Academy of Sciences' Institute of Mountain Hazards and Environment, told China's People's Daily Online.

Experts say the retreat of glaciers can cause glacial lakes to expand, increasing the risk of sudden, potentially devastating floods that can cross borders into countries such as Nepal, India and Bhutan. Several major rivers flowing through these countries originate on the Tibetan Plateau.

The plateau now has more than 14,000 glacial lakes, covering over 1,100 sq km, according to People's Daily.

A 2024 study published by the American Geophysical Union projected a significant rise in landslide hazards across the Himalayas and Tibet in the coming decades due to increased rainstorms.

While the largest absolute increases are expected in already vulnerable areas, including India's Garhwal and Kumaon regions and Nepal, the greatest relative increase is projected on the Tibetan Plateau.

The growing risks make co-operation more urgent. But past efforts by India and China to work together on Himalayan environmental issues have made little progress.

The two Asian powers have often found common ground at UN climate negotiations, pushing back against Western demands for emissions cuts and arguing that developing countries should not bear the same burden as industrialised nations.

Yet they have no dedicated agreement to jointly address the impacts of climate change in the Himalayas.

In 2009, India and China agreed to undertake joint research into the impact of global warming on glaciers in the Himalayas and Tibet.

Following a visit to Beijing, India's then environment minister Jairam Ramesh announced that the Wadia Institute of Himalayan Geology and China's Cold and Arid Regions Environmental and Engineering Research Institute would collaborate on the project.

But the initiative went nowhere, according to a scientist involved in the effort.

"One meeting was held between us and the Chinese side and that was it, nothing came out of it," said Dr DP Dobhal, a retired glaciologist who headed the glaciology programme at the Wadia Institute.

Since the early 2000s, India and China had agreements under which Beijing provided flood-season hydrological data on the Brahmaputra and Sutlej, two major rivers originating in Tibet.

But in August 2025, India's junior foreign minister Kirti Vardhan Singh told parliament that both agreements had expired. China had stopped sharing data on the Brahmaputra in June 2023, while India had received no data on the Sutlej since 2022.

China has not publicly explained the latest interruption. But when it withheld similar information in 2017, amid a tense military stand-off with India, Beijing blamed technical problems at its hydrological monitoring stations in Tibet, Singh said.

Some analysts see a glimmer of hope in the recent thaw between India and China, marked by high-level political engagement and moves to revive cross-border trade through Himalayan routes.

"These developments suggest there might be more room for the three countries to explore climate-related co-operation," says William Yang, senior analyst for North East Asia at the International Crisis Group.

But he says Beijing is likely to remain cautious about any major agreement with India and Nepal, as border disputes remain unresolved.

One major obstacle is that information vital for understanding climate risks can also have military value.

"What climate scientists might see as essential research data might look like strategic intelligence to the national security establishment in an environment where two militaries face each other across a disputed frontier," says Walter Ladwig, an associate fellow in the Indo-Pacific Programme at the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI), a UK-based defence and security think tank.

Such tensions have also hampered past efforts to tackle disasters that cross Himalayan borders.

The Kathmandu-based International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD) has spent more than three decades promoting regional co-operation, including on flood early-warning systems. But progress has been slow.

"There are certain highly sensitive issues in transboundary matters like comprehensive data of river flows that countries might not want to share, particularly upstream countries," says Arun Bhakta Shrestha, a former senior specialist at ICIMOD.

He says countries should instead focus on sharing less sensitive information about disaster risks.

Dr Uday Kala, head of the Centre for Climate Change and Disaster Management at India's IIT Mandi, suggests starting with practical steps - jointly identifying high-risk glacial lakes and cross-border hazards, agreeing on basic data-sharing protocols and monitoring standards, and exchanging critical warnings without delay.

"Climate change is moving the baseline itself; catching up with the previous disaster is no longer enough. We need to anticipate the next one," he says.

Whether India and China are willing to take even these steps remains uncertain.

For Nepal, the challenge is to convince its two powerful neighbours to put aside their differences and work together to tackle a shared climate threat.

items.title: How backlash against data centres could shape the US midterm elections
items.summary: Democrats and Republicans alike are coming out against data centre development, amid growing backlash across the US.
items.content:
A year ago, a longtime US senator was not thinking much about data centres. ​​

Now, according to one of his advisers, he is having regular meetings with staff to track their impact and working on new legislation aimed at curbing their rapid expansion across the country.

"This happens sometimes, something starts slow and then it goes fast," the senior policy adviser to the Democratic senator told the BBC. The person spoke on condition of anonymity as they are not permitted to speak to the press.

The 180-degree turn in this senator's attention was driven almost entirely by a growing wave of public backlash that has seen politicians across the country scramble to keep up. Public sentiment has turned against the expansion of data centres, the large warehouses that store processing power needed for internet activity.

Packed with rows and rows of computer chips, sometimes seven-feet high, data centres have turned into more than infrastructure for the internet. They are now the physical embodiment of the recent and explosive growth of artificial intelligence (AI) technology, and the varied fears people associate with it.

"I don't want to be the guinea pig for this," Indiana resident Angelita Soriano told the BBC.

A backlash over data centres is another threat to the AI juggernaut

A new Amazon data centre is being built directly across the street from her home. When complete, the 26-building structure will take up more than a square mile in her neighbourhood and maintain 782 diesel-powered generators.

Some data centres are even larger. In Ohio, a joint effort between OpenAI, Nvidia, SB Energy and the US Department of Energy is set to build a data centre complex that will stretch for roughly six square miles, the same size as most townships in the US.

There are about 3,000 data centres currently operating in the US, with that number potentially doubling in the next few years, according to a report by , external Pew Research Center.

Data centres are built through very local rules and permits, meaning federal lawmakers like US senators have little say in the process.

Yet, opposition has become so strong so quickly in the US that suddenly, politicians at all levels are now all but required to take a stand.

"This isn't just an issue on the left, there is huge pushback among conservatives to data centres," Chloe Autio, an AI policy adviser, said. "Whoever articulates a clear position and sticks to it, in either party, really stands to benefit."

Her analysis was echoed by the adviser to the US senator working on data centre legislation.

"There is a clear policy need here that we're looking to fill," he said. "This is a major backlash across the country - constituents are seeing the impacts of data centres and they do not like them."

That has put many on Capitol Hill - even Republicans - in direct conflict with President Donald Trump, who has championed the unrestrained growth of AI technology.

Trump has dubbed the backlash to data centres a "sick conspiracy" and said people and towns working to keep the buildings out are "backwards and poor".

His ire has been used as a boon to Democratic politicians looking to draw midterm votes from unhappy or undecided constituents.

The BBC spoke to residents of Indiana, Arizona, Michigan, Pennsylvania and Oregon, all of whom have been organising locally against the development of data centres. They expressed concerns about many aspects of the buildings, including their size, construction and operational noise, their impact on air, water and energy resources, as well as the speed at which they seem to be approved by local authorities.

During the first few months of this year, community groups organising against data centres more than doubled to 833, cropping up in almost every US state, according to research from Data Center Watch. The firm collects data for AI industry stakeholders and is part of an AI startup 10a Labs.

Stephanie Maldonado, the political director of LUCHA, a community organising group based in Arizona, referred to the pushback against data centres as "a David and Goliath story" that began several years ago.

"People have been ready to put a stop to it," Maldonado added. "Now, people are angry."

New national polling , external shows that AI regulation and data centres are among some of the top issues for voters this election cycle, behind the ongoing Iran war and various aspects of the economy.

Proponents of building data centres often argue the projects will create more, and better paying, local jobs.

Yet, recent research , external from the Brookings Institution, a non-partisan policy research group, found that a new data centre creates between 100 and 200 local jobs, which is "fewer than industry advocates claim". The projects also have essentially no impact on local wages.

Arizona Governor Katie Hobbs was one such proponent - until public pressure pushed her to the other side of the issue. In July, she enacted a three-year pause on any new tax break given to a company for a data centre project.

Arizona is far from the only state to see politicians react to data centre backlash.

Abdul El Sayed, a Democrat running for Senate in Michigan, made new rules and regulations for data centres a clear part of his successful primary campaign for Senate.

In the race for governor of Georgia, a Democrat who is calling for a pause on data centre development is in a dead heat with a Republican who disagrees.

Republican Senator John Husted of Ohio, who is fighting to keep his seat against Democrat Sherrod Brown, has also had to shift his position. Recent polls , external have found that the majority of Ohio voters oppose data centres. He has softened his support, saying that their arrival should be up to local citizens and elected officials.

Meanwhile, Brown has stumped on his opposition to new data centres. He leads Husted in recent polls.

Husted's trouble in Ohio led the National Republican Senatorial Committee, the major fundraising arm for conservatives in the Senate, to write in a private memo , external that Republican politicians needed to entirely reframe how they spoke to voters on data centres.

"This has become a sleeper issue for the entire election cycle," the NRSC added.

Texas is perhaps the most clear cut example of how backlash has turned into an undeniable issue for even the most pro-business politician.

The state currently has almost 300 operational data centres, with another 170 planned for development, according to Pew data.

At the end of last year, Republican Governor Greg Abbott had boasted of Texas as "the epicentre of AI development" because of the number of data centres it housed.

Within months he was backtracking, citing concerns of "safety and quality of life".

It could play a part in the state's upcoming Senate race too.

Democrat James Talarico's campaign is pushing for an end to "sweetheart tax deals" for Big Tech. He's now seen as a frontrunner for the historically Republican seat, where he is facing off against Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton.

Paxton said in a late September interview that there was still "plenty of open space in Texas that we can put data centres".

Many of the actions or proposals that have come from politicians looking to appease or address these voters are temporary. Most of the moratoriums, for instance, will end in one to three years.

It is possible that the political winds will have shifted by the time such moratoriums expire, leaving Big Tech and AI firms to build as they wish.

Balaji Tammabattula, the chief executive of Barupon, is developing a roughly 700-acre data centre and technology campus in Liberty, Texas. Despite the buildings being designed to use rain capture for water and supply its own energy needs, an increasingly common design for major data centre projects, Tammabattula told the BBC that people in the community oppose the project out of hand.

"There's just such a high level of tension from the jump that you can't really even break through with the facts," he said.

During a recent community event, Tammabattula said he tried to speak one-on-one with a woman who was vociferously opposed to the project.

"She just looked right at me and said, 'Get the hell out of my state.'"

items.title: How a Chinese-made toy gets to a US retailer
items.summary: With Christmas on the horizon, we trace children's toys from factories in China to US shelves.
items.content:
On the underside of most children's toys on sale in the US you'll find the same three words – "Made in China".

Nearly eight in 10 toys (78.3%) imported into the country in 2024 came from China, according to US government figures. , external

Last year, toys imported from China were worth $9.8bn (£7.4bn), trade figures show. , external

With Christmas on the horizon, the toy industry in the US and elsewhere is about to have its busiest time of the year by far.

As retailers prepare their stocks for the festive rush, be they online giants or "mom-and-pop" physical stores, the BBC World Service's Follow the Money series traces how a toy gets from a factory in China to the US. And where the money goes.

Guangdong province, which neighbours Hong Kong in southern China, is the heart of the country's toy manufacturing industry.

In the city of Dongguan workers on the floor of the Mihox factory pop plastic toys out of steel moulds, and pile them into crates ready for painting.

The company says it employs more than 800 people and makes around 55 million toys a year for the American market, which represents half of its business.

Follow the money: The journey of a $30 toy from China to America

Every toy starts with a design from a customer, such as an American toy company. The factory then makes a prototype, and builds moulds from which plastic parts and other components are formed.

Going from the first idea to finished toy takes one to two years, says Melanie Wang from the Mihox sales team. Much of that is the customer going back to the drawing board. "They modified the design again, again, and again to improve it."

Once the design is signed off, things move more quickly. A mould takes about a month to make, and the production run lasts about three months.

So, how much of the US retail price does the factory get? "About 20%," says Wang.

On a $30 toy, that's $6, which has to cover the price of the plastic and other materials, production costs including wages, and what profit the factory makes.

Chinese factories typically make a profit of between 3% and 10%, according to Jay Foreman, chief executive of US toy firm Basic Fun. So for a $30 toy that's between 60 and 18 cents of the $6 the factory charges to make it.

Samson Ko is president of the Toys Manufacturers' Association of Hong Kong. Many of his members moved their factories across the border into mainland China in the 1980s, attracted by cheaper land and labour.

He says the way toys are made has barely changed since then. "Automation now takes place mostly in the moulding and the packaging process. But for soft toys, or even some of the electronics nowadays, it's still very labour intensive."

And Chinese labour isn't cheap anymore, he adds, after recent rises.

Average pay in Vietnam is about half of that in China, said one report , external at the start of this year.

Yet fewer than 10% of Ko's members have moved any production outside China, and in those cases mostly only because customers asked them to do so.

The Chinese factories remain busy, he says, because a single toy can undergo more than one manufacturing process, from moulding the parts, to adding electronics, sewing materials, and final assembly. This often requires it travelling to different factories.

Ko adds that in Guangdong these separate facilities are located close to each other, and used to "working in harmony". He says this makes the whole manufacturing process run more smoothly than in other countries.

From the factory, the toy goes by truck to a port, such as Shenzhen, the biggest in Guangdong.

Ivy Tse is co-founder of FreightAmigo, a Hong Kong logistics company that runs an online platform for both Hong Kong and mainland China exporters. These businesses can book a cargo container, sea passage to an overseas destination, arrange insurance cover, and secure finance.

Tse says it takes about 15 days for a cargo ship to get from Shenzhen to the US west coast, and 25 to 30 days to the east coast. This year's Christmas toys left China in August and September.

Freight, from factory to the US, usually adds about 10% to the manufacturing cost of a toy, adds Tse. So if we stick to a toy that retails for $30 in the US, and therefore costs $6 to make in China, the cost of getting it to the states is 60 cents.

Once the toy reaches the US there is currently a tariff on Chinese toys that has to be paid to the US Customs and Border Protection (CBP).

Following talks between President Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping last month, the two governments have recommended toys for lower tariffs. But no new rate or start date has been set, and the US must first hold a public consultation. For now the basic rate is 12.5%, and some toys pay more.

This is charged on the manufacturing price of the toy, not on how much it retails for. So for a $30 toy, that basic rate is 12.5% of $6, which is 75 cents.

This tariff is paid for by the American company that has imported the toys. One such firm is Learning Resources, a family business based near Chicago that sells educational toys. Half of these it imports from China.

"We pay 100% of the tariffs, let there be no doubt about that," says the company's chief executive Rick Woldenberg.

The cost of making the $30 toy, getting it to the US, and paying the import tariff, comes to $7.35. So that leaves $22.65, or 75.5% of the total.

That money never leaves the US, explains Foreman from Basic Fun. His firm, which is based in Florida, makes Tonka trucks and Care Bears cuddly toys.

"It's kept by my company, the [US] transportation company, the retailer," he says.

If we allow $2.65 for the US delivery firm, the toy company and the retailer will typically share the remaining revenues 50-50. So that would give them $10 each.

While profit margins are commercially sensitive and therefore not generally revealed, industry studies show that the toy firm and retailer would usually make a profit of up to 25% or $2.50.

Getting a toy onto the shelves in the US requires both a lot of work and a long journey.

items.content:
My friend and I are huge Neovim nerds. We like to rice our terminals and our editors. We just wanted a harness that we can do the same with, rice it till our hearts' desire. So, we started looking out for harnesses. Pi was great, Pi was good. But in the end, it was JavaScript. I don't have anything against JavaScript, but Lua is more fitting, and I can just as easily base it in Rust to make it even faster. So, we started cooking, and we ended up with a design that's minimal at its core and is built using Lua. Every built-in abstraction, the way you define providers, the way you rice it up, everything, literally everything, you can do in Lua.

But how? How does it all work? I proposed we just do it the Ratatui way, but my friend was like, nah! We shall make it possible to build TUIs in Lua. (Weirdo!) But it paid off, and we got ourselves a shiny new Lua library, ito!!!

He didn't get the gravity of the situation. We had an awesome terminal UI library in Lua! I wanted everyone to know how cool that is, so I got cooking, wrote myself a custom canvas implementation of this library instead of the usual terminal adaptor, exported it as wasm, and made this super cool website where you can experiment building awesome UIs in Lua. For vibe-coders, we got an llms.txt too. Have at it, and see if you can build something really cool with it. The library's at github.com/uji-labs/ito, and the awesome sauce harness is at github.com/uji-labs/uji.

I hope you like it!

items.title: At the Brooklyn novelty shop in 'surreal' row with Kelly Clarkson over mechanical bird
items.summary: Art of Play says its staff have been threatened after the singer complained online about how she was treated.
items.content:
On a rainy Wednesday afternoon, a novelty toy and games store in a quiet part of New York City was seeing much busier foot traffic than usual.

Inside, the shop was packed with cameramen and customers, while passersby in this Brooklyn neighbourhood of Cobble Hill looked inside, asking: "Where's the bird?"

Art of Play has found itself at the centre of a social media storm since the weekend when Grammy-winning musician Kelly Clarkson complained online that the boutique store would not let her buy a singing and dancing mechanical bird that was perched on the wall.

The Since U Been Gone singer claimed she was "looked at as if I couldn't afford" the bird - which she said had a price tag of $15,000 (£11,000).

"Y'all should go check out Art of Play in Brooklyn if you enjoy being treated like Julia Roberts' character in Pretty Woman," she said, referring to a scene from the 1990 romantic comedy film where Roberts' character is treated poorly by staff at a shop, who imply she cannot afford various items.

In a follow-up post on social media, Clarkson said the store had told her the bird cost $15,000 and that they could find her something else "comparable".

Art of Play has defended how it treated the star on social media, saying the wooden bird - which is called Molly - is permanently attached to the wall and is not for sale.

It said that during Clarkson's five-minute visit on Saturday, an employee suggested to her that she could buy an identical bird for $15,000.

They also said they had offered her a different singing bird for $2,000 from a clock-making shop in Germany, which she could have purchased that day.

"Imagine our surprise when our small local business was suddenly attacked by eight million people who have never visited our store," Art of Play said.

"It's been a surreal experience to be the focus of such widespread outrage after just one mention by a celebrity."

Clarkson defended her decision to criticise the store on social media, saying: "I never blast people but you my friend were an exception."

When the BBC visited the store on Wednesday, there were more reporters than customers.

A shopkeeper said they would not comment on the story anymore and just wanted to get back to business as usual.

Molly still hung on the wall at the shop, this time next to a price tag of $15m.

The sign jokes that the sculpture is the "world's most famous singing bird automata!"

The store's owner has said he and his staff have faced threats and harassment after Clarkson's complaint, telling the BBC's US partner CBS News that the singer had endangered them.

This week, a man filmed himself yelling expletives outside the store, before accusing its employees of "racially profiling" Clarkson.

The kerfuffle lingered in headlines on Wednesday as a news outlet released surveillance video from Art of Play purporting to show Clarkson's visit.

The grainy footage, which has no audio, is said to show her wearing a yellow shirt, a baseball cap and a backpack while browsing items, including Molly the bird.

She can be seen talking with an employee - apparently about the bird as she points at it - and later moving to leave the store. She comes back in to say something animatedly to the cashier.

But while the argument over the bird has gone viral online, some of Art of Play's customers had not heard about it before being greeted by news cameras on the premises.

One customer who was in town visiting his daughter said he was not familiar with the controversy.

For others, Clarkson's claims that those at the store had treated her rudely came as a surprise.

Kiran Ramineni, who lives next door, described Art of Play as a "very nice small mom and pop store" and said he had seen flocks of journalists there in recent days.

Shopgoer Emily Trantanella, 27, said: "I feel like a pretty woman and I've always been treated very well here.

items.title: Guerra Ucraina - Russia. Romania, a fuoco due petroliere nel Mar Nero. Dan: “Colpite da droni russi nel nostro spazio aereo”
items.summary: Media di Kiev: Starlink ha ripreso a funzionare. Raid ucraini su impianto a Ryazan. Perquisito e fermato il caporedattore di Novaya Gazeta. In corso il Consiglio europeo, Metsola: “Il Cremlino intensifica gli attacchi, l'Ue non distolga lo sguardo”
items.content:
Le due petroliere che hanno preso fuoco durante la notte nel Mar Nero, nelle acque territoriali rumene, sono state colpite da droni russi entrati nello spazio aereo del Paese. Lo spiega il presidente rumeno Nicusor Dan, come riporta Sky News. Otto persone risultano disperse.

Le due petroliere erano all’ancora nel Mar Nero, vicino alla foce di un canale che sfocia nel Danubio, quando le autorità navali rumene hanno ricevuto il primo allarme di emergenza dalla petroliera Wine Trader, battente bandiera di San Marino. Successivamente anche la petroliera Yara J, battente bandiera delle Comore, ha preso fuoco.

Presidente rumeno, le due petroliere a fuoco nel Mar Nero per droni russi nel nostro spazio aereo

Cremlino: “Distruttiva la posizione dei Paesi europei sull'accordo per il gasolio”

Il Cremlino: “Il diesel sta iniziando a tornare sui mercati globali”

Metsola: “Mosca intensifica gli attacchi su Kiev, l'Ue non distolga lo sguardo”

Tajani: “Importante che l’Europa serve un portavoce comune per trattare sull’Ucraina, si decida in tempi rapidi”

Zelensky al Ft: “Riprenderemo gli attacchi alle raffinerie russe”

Il presidente ucraino, Volodymyr Zelensky, ha denunciato un "orribile attacco russo" con un drone 'Shahed' a getto "contro un semplice negozio" nella regione di Odessa, dove si sono registrati tre feriti. "La Russia continua il suo sanguinoso terrore. Il negozio è stato parzialmente distrutto e alcune automobili sono state danneggiate", ha scritto su X il leader di Kiev, sottolineando che "i servizi di emergenza sono al lavoro sul posto e stanno prestando assistenza". "E' importante che i nostri partner ci aiutino a difenderci", ha proseguito, "edifici residenziali, negozi, infrastrutture energetiche e altre infrastrutture critiche sono sotto attacco praticamente senza sosta. Non c'è un'ora di pace". "Ciò che sta accadendo è la risposta deliberata della Russia ai segnali che sta ricevendo dall'America. Purtroppo, stanno arrivando segnali pericolosi sulla possibilità di un ulteriore allentamento delle sanzioni", ha poi denunciato Zelensky.

L'abitazione del caporedattore di Novaya Gazeta, Sergei Sokolov , è stata perquisita e lo stesso giornalista è attualmente in fase di trasferimento presso il Comitato Investigativo per essere interrogato. E' quanto riportato dalla stessa testata. "I contatti con Sokolov si sono interrotti intorno alle 12:15 ora di Mosca. I suoi telefoni risultano disattivati", si legge sul canale Telegram di Novaya Gazeta. Fonti di Rbk e di Rt nelle forze dell'ordine hanno riferito che le perquisizioni sono collegate al caso del giornalista di Novaya Gazeta, Oleg Roldugin, aperto in primavera.

Presidente rumeno, le due petroliere a fuoco nel Mar Nero per droni russi nel nostro spazio aereo

Le due petroliere che hanno preso fuoco durante la notte nel Mar Nero, nelle acque territoriali rumene, sono state colpite da droni russi entrati nello spazio aereo del Paese. Lo spiega il presidente rumeno Nicusor Dan, come riporta Sky News. Otto persone risultano disperse. Le due petroliere erano all'ancora nel Mar Nero, vicino alla foce di un canale che sfocia nel Danubio, quando le autorità navali rumene hanno ricevuto il primo allarme di emergenza dalla petroliera Wine Trader, battente bandiera di San Marino. Successivamente anche la petroliera Yara J, battente bandiera delle Comore, ha preso fuoco.

Cremlino: “Distruttiva la posizione dei Paesi europei sull'accordo per il gasolio”

I Paesi europei hanno assunto "una posizione distruttiva" sull'accordo tra Donald Trump e Vladimir Putin per l'export di gasolio russo. Lo ha detto il portavoce del Cremlino, Dmitry Peskov. "Non solo non hanno accolto questo accordo, ma lo hanno criticato aspramente", ha sottolineato Peskov, citato da Interfax. "Attualmente, i mercati energetici e i mercati petroliferi globali si trovano in una situazione molto tesa", ha aggiunto Peskov, sottolineando che "molti fattori influenzano questa situazione negativa, tra cui, ovviamente, l'impossibilità per la Russia di esportare significative quantità di petrolio e prodotti petroliferi".

Gli "sforzi energici degli Stati Uniti per assicurare una soluzione pacifica del conflitto in Ucraina si stanno infrangendo contro la mancanza di volontà di Kiev e, personalmente, di Zelensky di giungere alla pace". Lo ha dichiarato il portavoce del Cremlino, Dmitry Peskov.

Il Cremlino: “Il diesel sta iniziando a tornare sui mercati globali”

Il diesel russo sta iniziando a tornare sui mercati internazionali, con possibili effetti positivi sulla stabilizzazione del mercato petrolifero. Lo ha dichiarato il portavoce del Cremlino Dmitry Peskov , citato da Ria Novosti. "Attualmente si stanno rendendo disponibili quantità piuttosto consistenti di diesel, che ha iniziato ad arrivare sui mercati mondiali. Questo avrà un certo effetto positivo sulla stabilizzazione dei mercati petroliferi", ha affermato Peskov, precisando tuttavia che il ritorno del carburante russo "non sarà sufficiente a stabilizzarli completamente, e bisogna esserne consapevoli".

Starshield in Motion, la versione militare del sistema di comunicazione satellitare americano Starlink, ha ripreso a funzionare. Lo sostengono fonti del ministero della Difesa ucraina sentite da Ukrainska Pravda. "A partire da ora, il lavoro di Starshield è ripreso e continua (a migliorare), lo stiamo registrando in base ai rapporti delle unità", affermano le fonti aggiungendo che "il ministero della Difesa sta inoltre continuando a comunicare per chiarire tutte le ragioni e le circostanze delle restrizioni di ieri".

A quanto si apprende da fonti Nato, oggi a Bruxelles il presidente ucraino Vlodomyr Zelensky incontrerà il segretario generale della Nato Mark Rutte. Zelensky è atteso domani alla seconda giornata di lavori del Consiglio europeo che discuterà il sostegno a Kiev.

L’appello di Zelensky: “Usa non si schierino con l’aggressore”

Il presidente ucraino, Volodymyr Zelensky , ha lanciato un nuovo appello agli Stati Uniti affinchè "non si schierino dalla parte dell'aggressore". "E' evidente che la Russia ha scelto deliberatamente di intensificare gli attacchi dopo aver beneficiato di un allentamento delle sanzioni e aver riscontrato tentativi di esercitare pressioni sull'Ucraina", ha scritto su X il leader di Kiev. "La Russia sfrutta ogni occasione di questo tipo e deve essere chiamata a rispondere delle proprie azioni. Sono necessarie decisioni coraggiose per porre fine a questa guerra", ha aggiunto.

Emergency services are still providing assistance in dozens of our cities and communities. Repair crews and rescuers are working to deal with the aftermath of Russian attacks. For practically all of yesterday and throughout last night, a massive “shahed” attack was underway. The drones kept coming in waves, and there was not a single hour when our skies were clear of them. From midnight yesterday through 9 a.m. today, there had already been more than 850 “shaheds” – and this comes precisely at a time when the speed of our defensive capabilities is being artificially restricted. We managed to shoot down some of the “shaheds.” But unfortunately, there were also dozens of hits. One of the largest attacks was carried out against our Kirovohrad region. There were also strikes in Kyiv and the surrounding region, the Dnipro, Odesa, Rivne, Kharkiv, Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia, Kherson, Mykolaiv, Vinnytsia, Zhytomyr, Khmelnytskyi, Poltava, and Ivano-Frankivsk regions. Three people were killed in Kropyvnytskyi and three more in the Dnipro region. My condolences to their families and loved ones. It is obvious that Russia deliberately chose to escalate its attacks after receiving sanctions relief and seeing attempts to pressure Ukraine. Russia exploits every such opportunity and must be held accountable for what it does. Strong decisions are needed to end this war. Ukraine needs steady support, above all in defending our skies. We need HONESTY from our partners about this war: It is important that everyone in America stand not with the aggressor, but with our efforts to protect lives, end this war, and guarantee security.

"L'Ucraina ha bisogno di un sostegno costante innanzitutto per la difesa dei propri cieli", ha poi concluso Zelensky, avvertendo che l'Ucraina si aspetta dai suoi partner "onestà riguardo al conflitto: è fondamentale che, in America, tutti scelgano di non stare dalla parte dell'aggressore, bensì di sostenere i nostri sforzi per proteggere le vite umane, porre fine alla guerra e garantire la sicurezza".

Le autorità rumene hanno avviato operazioni di ricerca e salvataggio al largo della costa del Mar Nero, in seguito a un incendio scoppiato a bordo di una nave. Otto persone risultano disperse mentre quattro sono state tratte in salvo. Le cause dell'incendio a bordo della "Wine Trader", una nave cisterna per prodotti chimici battente bandiera di San Marino, in viaggio dalla Tunisia verso la Romania, non sono ancora chiare. Tuttavia, una recente serie di attacchi con droni contro imbarcazioni nel Mar Nero ha sollevato il timore che la guerra in Ucraina, scatenata dalla Russia, possa estendersi ulteriormente.

items.title: La principessa di Norvegia e il marito sciamano fanno causa ad amici e parenti: “Ci hanno diffamato”
items.summary: La coppia chiede un risarcimento milionario a chi avrebbe, tra l’altro, rivelato al tabloid norvegese Se og Hør notizie in merito all’accusa di presunta violenza sessuale ai danni di Durek Verret
items.content:
Ottanta milioni di dollari, ovvero 71 milioni di euro. Tanto avrebbero perso la Principessa e lo sciamano in termini di accordi saltati, per via delle malignità che sul loro conto avrebbero detto amici, parenti e stretti collaboratori, persone cioè della loro cerchia più intima. Così, hanno deciso di intraprendere un’ azione legale presentando una denuncia formale presso i tribunali statunitensi cinque giorni dopo la scomparsa del padre della Principessa, Harald V di Norvegia , e tre giorni dopo la morte della sorella del Re, la principessa Astrid. "Avremmo preferito dedicare questo tempo alla nostra salute, alla famiglia, al lutto e alla guarigione", hanno fatto sapere i querelanti, dicendo tuttavia di essere stati costretti dalle “scadenze legali” ad agire per vie legali “in questo momento inopportuno".

Märtha Louise e il marito Durek Verrett avrebbero deciso di far causa a un gruppo significativo di persone per diffamazione e violazione degli accordi di riservatezza . Sono in tutto 14 le persone accusate dalla coppia attraverso la sua società, Ohana Productions LLC, e tra loro c’è anche una parente : Demetria Farmer Oster, sorellastra di Durek Verrett. Secondo la coppia, la donna e altri avrebbero diffuso false informazioni che avrebbero gravemente danneggiato la loro reputazione . In particolare, Verrett sostiene che alcuni ex collaboratori abbiano "diffuso informazioni, registrazioni audio e accuse" sui social media, su internet e sulla stampa norvegese, causando "significative conseguenze finanziarie". Il suo reddito sarebbe infatti "crollato" e "opportunità e inviti a conferenze, partecipazioni a programmi televisive, sponsorizzazioni e simili collaborazioni commerciali” si sarebbero significativamente ridotte. Alcuni impegni sarebbero stati addirittura annullati.

Märtha Louise è la figlia maggiore di Harald V e della regina Sonja , ma non è mai stata erede al trono perché la legge di successione norvegese è stata modificata dopo la sua nascita, senza azione retroattiva, quindi alla morte di suo padre è diventato Re suo fratello minore, Haakon . Che ha non pochi problemi, al momento, tra la malattia cronica di sua moglie Mette-Marit , sottoposta nel giugno scorso a un trapianto di polmone, e la condanna per stupro e violenza domestica che pende sul figliastro Marius Borg Høiby, che in attesa di revisione del processo sconta i domiciliare nella tenuta del Palazzo Reale.

Märtha Louise ha rassegnato le sue “dimissioni dalla famiglia reale” – rinunciato al trattamento di Sua Altezza Reale – nel 2002 e si è ritirata dai suoi doveri come membro attivo della famiglia reale 20 anni dopo; resta Principessa per nascita, ma non può usare il suo titolo per motivi commerciali. In Norvegia, è stata accusata di aver oltrepassato questo limite in diverse occasioni. La sua relazione con Durek Verret è stata criticata fin dagli esordi, perché l’uomo – sciamano per professione, negli Usa – è stato descritto come un impostore ; cosa che la coppia torna a denunciare, sostenendo che la copertura mediatica della loro relazione “abbia suggerito che il sostegno di Märtha Louise a Verrett fosse dovuto a un'influenza psicologica piuttosto che al suo giudizio personale", scrive il quotidiano norvegese Se og Hør , che ha avuto accesso al testo integrale della denuncia. La principessa e suo marito sostengono che il comportamento dei media sarebbe stato "ripugnante e persistente", soprattutto nel corso del 2025 e del 2026, ovvero nel periodo più delicato per la coppia, tra cui la grave insufficienza renale che ha costretto Durek alla dialisi e poi a un trapianto di rene , nonché l’aggravarsi delle condizioni di Re Harald e la sua scomparsa.

La coppia chiede insomma un risarcimento ai querelati pari a 80 milioni di dollari (oltre 71 milioni di euro) , così distribuiti: 30 milioni di dollari (circa 26,8 milioni di euro) a Durek Verrett e 30 milioni di dollari alla sua azienda, più 20 milioni (circa 17,8 milioni di euro) per la principessa. la sorella del re Haakon VIII, che afferma di aver subito perdite finanziarie, ne chiede 20 milioni (circa 17,8 milioni di euro). "La reputazione dei nostri clienti è stata giudicata dall'opinione pubblica per anni. D'ora in poi, i fatti saranno esaminati in tribunale", hanno fatto sapere gli avvocati americani della coppia, Richard Roth e Jamie Campbell. L'udienza è fissata a Los Angeles per dicembre.

Tra le accuse più gravi e infamanti riportate dalla stampa norvegese c’è quella rivolta contro Durek Verrett: il tabloid Se og Hør ha pubblicato la testimonianza di un uomo svedese di 49 anni che accusava Durek Verrett di presunti abusi sessuali risalenti al 2015, avvenuti durante una sessione di guarigione olistica. La coppia si è rivolta al PFU – Pressens Faglige Utvalg, ovvero al consiglio norvegese per l'etica nella stampa, per condannare il tabloid, che in effetti è stato redarguito per non aver verificato a fondo le accuse e per aver pubblicato un'immagine non autorizzata di Verrett.

La principessa Märtha Louise di Norvegia è madre di tre figlie: Maud Angelica (2003), Leah Isadora (2005) ed Emma Tallulah (2008), nate dal suo primo matrimonio con lo scrittore Ari Behn, orto suicida. Ha sposato in seconde nozze Verret il ​​31 agosto 2024, con la famiglia reale norvegese presente al completo, e l’anno successivo assieme a lui raccontato la sua “vera storia” in un documentario Netflix, come hanno fatto Harry e Meghan, dal titolo "Rebel Royals: The Unlikely Romance" .

items.title: We’re releasing Jev 1.14.0 along with experimental features for dreamers
items.summary: Article URL: https://typesafe.ai/blog/jev-1-14 Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50095353 Points: 318 # Comments: 102
items.content:
TL;DR: We're releasing an improved Jev 1.14.0 along with experimental features for our dreamers: images, a new type, and longer context. Enter the danger zone at your own risk. 🔥

A huge debate we’ve been having is on the balance between reliability and creativity.

To really care about the prod builders, we should be shipping models that meet our quality bar for intelligence and have been battle-tested to the limits of what we can do internally.

On the other hand, there’s no way that our team has a full understanding of what is needed to spark delight in the world and build sick sci-fi. We don’t want to impose our values of extreme reliability on those dreamers.

Our solution: share those dreamer-ready features under “danger zone” flags in our API headers. These are features that will be here to stay for future models, are (as far as we can tell) better than what exists out there, and will continue to get better by leaps and bounds. But as a warning, we think there is still way too much jaggedness for us to vouch for these for production use cases!

See these new capabilities as a continuation of what we’ve built over 2 years of stealth. They’re less ready for automation, but very fun to play with. They’re also an early glimpse into what we’re focused on making reliable enough to meet TypeSafe standards.

Not only are we enabling multimodality for future Jev models, we’re enabling it for the current Jev that you all know and love. Surprise: the Jev you all know and love ( jev-1.13.0 ) was multimodal all along!

Image support is fully composable via a find-and-replace in assets . You can put them anywhere that our JSON interface supports: in the state , instructions , or even criteria ! Play around with it, push the boundaries of technology, and let us know where Jev can improve.

As a warning, all models (Jev included) perform worse on multimodality over pure text. Breaking down questions into the simplest possible decompositions helps a lot.

We’re introducing another new type as well: box . It returns a single bounding box - no type errors allowed. It’s our first type that’s not purely meant for smart-if statements, and is a preview for our explorations beyond simple decisions into what else System One Models can support.

We made huge leaps and bounds on this one recently, so we’re enabling this only for jev-1.14.0 (spoilers).

We’ve heard you loud and clear on context lengths. Jev actually supports a much longer context length than we’ve enabled in production. We chose to limit it intentionally because Jev, like all models, is less reliable on longer contexts, and this constraint encourages more effective usage patterns in prod.

We aren’t your parents though, so while we strongly recommend limiting context length, you no longer have to:

We love the community’s desire to help make models better! We’ve added an opt-in to allow you to help find model jaggedness with your queries. We will still not train on your queries, but this does make it easier for us to find issues and help debug your use cases.

We’re also releasing a new version of Jev under jev-preview ! Not meant to be flashy but instead be small, subtle improvements to everything . Most things should be a tiny bit better, but we expect the largest gain in multi-lingual support.

Model releases should generally also be strict improvements, but we’re well aware of how much developers hate updating their dependencies. jev-latest will be updated to jev-1.14.0 in a week. jev-1.13.0 will be available for a while.

We intend to give 60 days warning before jev-1.13.0 is formally deprecated, and 30 days for jev-1.14.0 . We’ll release a deprecation policy prior to this.

As you all know, we dislike public benchmarks . However, we have our own internal best guesses on how to measure the form factor of intelligence that matters most for developers.

We’re trying something new out here: we’re going to treat you guys like adults and share this with you all.

This measurement is our best guess and will continue to evolve. If ever we show you our internal numbers again, don’t expect them to be consistent.

Don’t believe it entirely. Always favor your own experimentation and evals with your use cases.

We’re including only open weight models because we guard our validation set very closely and are spooked out about the data policies of our model providers.

This is likely biased towards our models. Feel free to ignore our model, and instead focus on the relative ranking of open source models.

Lots of people love to ask what kind of sci-fi we’re releasing next. While we are working on some mindblowing stuff, expect most releases to be beautifully boring (like we think AI should be): small improvements across the board, better stability, and features for real deployment.

items.title: Student protesters attack government buildings in Albania
items.summary: Buildings were set alight on the second day of demonstrations from thousands of students who want better university conditions and job prospects.
items.content:
Thousands of students have taken to the streets in the Albanian capital of Tirana, attacking several government buildings on the second day of violent anti-government protests.

The demonstration began outside the ministry of education on Tuesday, as students called for better university conditions and job prospects.

Wednesday saw part of the education ministry's building set on fire, while the prime minister's office, finance and interior ministry, and several surrounding businesses were also attacked.

Albania's Deputy Prime Minister ​Albana Koçiu has called for "calmness, self-restraint and maturity" and said "Albania does not need to burn to change".

Riot police have clashed with the protesters, using tear gas and water cannons to disperse them.

One demonstrator, Enida Bimi, told Reuters news agency that the protest is not just for the students, but "for all the people of Albania".

"The people are very angry at the system. They need to change everything. With this corruption all around, the crime and everything else is happening. And the people now are angry. They need to change the system," Bimi said.

Another protester, Arber Leshi, said people are angry at "the most corrupt government our country has ever seen".

Education Mirela Kumbaro said that while she respects the right to protest, "civic student protest and violence against public buildings and property are two different things".

"Setting fire to an institution is not a peaceful protest. It is an act that endanger's peoples lives", said economy minister Delina Ibrahimaj, responding to a video appearing to show protesters throwing rocks at the finance ministry building.

Sixteen people were arrested "in connection with violent acts" during Tuesday's protest, Albania's state-run news agency said.

Sali Berisha, the leader of the opposition - the Democratic Party of Albania - has praised the protesters.

"The streets and squares of Tirana have never seen lions like these students," he said during an evening meeting on Wednesday, Albania's state-run news agency Ata reported.

This student-led protest comes after months of anti-government protests, known as the Flamingo Revolution , which is calling for Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama to resign.

The protests were sparked by a luxury tourism project linked to Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner , which fuelled anger over alleged corruption and a lack of transparency from Rama's government.

'Flamingo Revolution' takes off as thousands demand Albanian PM's resignation

Kushner-backed luxury resort plan sparks protests in Albania

items.title: Per il secondo giorno consecutivo in Albania gli studenti hanno protestato danneggiando la sede del ministero dell’Istruzione
items.content:
Mercoledì a Tirana, capitale dell’Albania, decine di migliaia di studenti hanno protestato contro il governo. Le manifestazioni erano iniziate martedì in modo pacifico, mentre oggi gli studenti si sono radunati davanti al ministero dell’Istruzione e alcuni di loro hanno lanciato dei sassi contro l’edificio danneggiando le ringhiere e hanno incendiato dei bidoni della spazzatura. La polizia è intervenuta con cannoni ad acqua e gas lacrimogeni per disperdere i manifestanti. Reuters , citando un testimone, scrive che sono state danneggiate anche due banche vicine al ministero. La polizia ha detto di aver arrestato circa 40 persone.

Gli studenti protestano contro le condizioni delle università, ritenute scadenti e troppo costose, e le scarse prospettive lavorative e di stipendio dopo la laurea. In generale gli studenti denunciano la corruzione della classe politica e chiedono le dimissioni del primo ministro Edi Rama.

A giugno in Albania c’erano già state grosse proteste contro la costruzione di un resort di lusso legato alla società di Jared Kushner, marito di Ivanka Trump e genero di Donald Trump, che si erano via via trasformate nelle più grandi manifestazioni antigovernative della storia recente del paese.

items.title: Things to know when you get cancer
items.summary: Article URL: https://jjmaxwell4.com/writing/things-to-know-when-you-get-cancer/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50093568 Points: 1568 # Comments: 375
items.content:
I was diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma in my mouth in May 2026. Here are some things I learned based on that experience so far.

Note, since this is on the front page of Hacker News right now. exhilaration suggested that if you are within a 2-3 hour drive of a major cancer center, go there instead of your local community hospital. Use the US News cancer hospital rankings . The top centers usually take your insurance, so use vacation days and book a hotel if you have to. The largest benefit I saw was speed. At MD Anderson I got a question answered within 20 minutes of a visit, because the doctor called the pathologist who he was on a first name basis with. If that wasn’t at a cancer center, it would have taken days, or more likely the question never would have been answered at all (I had asked my oncologist about this and he’d just shrugged). The rest of the HN comments are worth reading too.

items.title: Zelensky dice di sentirsi tradito da Trump
items.summary: Lo accusa di essersi schierato con la Russia e sostiene che gli Stati Uniti abbiano limitato deliberatamente Starlink
items.content:
Il presidente ucraino Volodymyr Zelensky ha detto di sentirsi tradito dal presidente statunitense Donald Trump per le sue ultime decisioni sulla guerra in Ucraina, tra cui l’accordo per consentire alla Russia di esportare più gasolio e l’annuncio di un “cessate il fuoco energetico” che la Russia non ha rispettato.

Nel corso di un’intervista con il giornalista britannico Piers Morgan ha anche accusato gli Stati Uniti e SpaceX, l’azienda proprietaria di Starlink, di aver limitato deliberatamente il servizio, impedendo all’esercito ucraino di svolgere alcune operazioni militari. «È un grave errore», ha detto Zelensky, aggiungendo che la decisione causerà molti morti.

Le limitazioni sono iniziate martedì notte e hanno riguardato in particolare il funzionamento dei droni che si muovono ad alta velocità. Le forze ucraine sono state costrette ad annullare diverse operazioni militari: sia di attacco contro le forze russe, sia di difesa dai droni russi. Zelensky ha detto di essere convinto che le limitazioni siano state introdotte consapevolmente dal governo statunitense e da SpaceX, e ha chiesto che il servizio venga ripristinato il prima possibile.

Nell’intervista Zelensky ha parlato più in generale del peggioramento dei rapporti con gli Stati Uniti. Alla domanda se si sentisse tradito per quanto accaduto negli ultimi giorni ha risposto di sì, aggiungendo però che «è un po’ più complicato di una questione di emozioni o sentimenti».

La crisi attuale nei rapporti tra Ucraina e Stati Uniti era iniziata d’improvviso la scorsa settimana, quando Trump aveva annunciato un accordo col presidente russo Vladimir Putin che sospendeva le sanzioni contro la Russia sulle esportazioni di gasolio, per consentire alla Russia di immetterne sul mercato mondiale e americano e fare così abbassare i prezzi. La questione del prezzo dell’energia è un tema centrale nel dibattito politico americano e importante per Trump, che tra tre settimane affronterà le elezioni di metà mandato negli Stati Uniti.

Trump aveva anche attaccato direttamente Zelensky: ne aveva chiesto la sostituzione e aveva iniziato a fare molte pressioni per interrompere del tutto gli attacchi ucraini alle infrastrutture e alle raffinerie russe. Secondo alcune ricostruzioni giornalistiche, aveva anche minacciato il governo ucraino di sospendere la condivisione delle informazioni di intelligence, con gravi conseguenze sulla possibilità di contenere i danni degli attacchi aerei e avvisare per tempo la popolazione civile.

La condivisione è stata poi effettivamente interrotta negli ultimi due giorni, insieme alle limitazioni alla connessione di Starlink . L’ipotesi più probabile è che siano entrambi strumenti di ricatto con cui l’amministrazione Trump sta cercando di costringere l’Ucraina a sospendere gli attacchi alle infrastrutture energetiche russe.

Secondo fonti del ministero della Difesa ucraino citate da Ukrinform , mercoledì sera la connessione ha ricominciato a funzionare fino a circa 160 chilometri orari, mentre durante la giornata si interrompeva anche a velocità molto inferiori, intorno agli 80 chilometri orari. Resta però il limite per le velocità maggiori, che ostacola soprattutto le operazioni con i droni intercettori, che devono raggiungere velocità elevate per inseguire e abbattere quelli russi.

items.content:
Hi HN!

I’m Jason Thomas, one of the founders of CoScreen.

As some of you may know, Datadog sunset the CoScreen service on July 31st.

Four of us from the original CoScreen team have spent the last couple months building a free and open source pair programming tool inspired by those that came before us: It’s called Petal (https://github.com/kiruna-labs/petal)

Some history first, because when we started CoScreen we had hoped to break the sad and established pattern of this industry.

Screenhero was an exceptional tool that a lot of us loved for pairing. Multiple cursors, low latency, you could click your partner’s editor, and just start typing. It felt like magic while we had it. Then Slack bought it in 2015, and shut down the standalone app in December 2017.

When Till, Max, and I started CoScreen, we were aware of this history, and wanted to build an even more magical collaboration and screen sharing experience: the entire concept was “throw a window from your laptop up on someone else’s screen, and start collaborating with zero friction.”

Datadog acquired us in 2022, and thus began the great adventure of adapting our real-time technology into Datadog products, while also continue developing CoScreen as a standalone tool from the Datadog ecosystem. Datadog invested in the product for years and we’re thankful for that. But CoScreen itself proved, like so many other screen sharing tool acquisitions, to be too tangential from the customer base and core mission. We instead built other communication features in Datadog, the integrations with other video platforms, and also its wildly successful MCP server. We weren't the only ones. Around was bought by Miro and shut down in March 2025. Multi (formerly Remotion) was acqui-hired by OpenAI in 2024 and shut down about a month later. It's nearly always the same story: a small team builds something hard that people love, a platform buys it for the team or the feature, and the standalone product doesn't survive the integration. So we decided firmly to do things differently this time. Petal is completely free and open source and we aren't monetizing it. If we lose interest or get hit by a bus, you can self-host it or fork it, and nobody can sunset it on you. Honestly it's a love letter to everyone in this community that supported us, believed in us, and to liberate collaborative screen sharing from this vicious cycle.

We hope through this we can help foster a large and vibrant community around innovating in this product sector. What Petal does: shared windows show up as real windows on your desktop, movable and resizable, not tiles in a grid. Several people can share at once, everyone gets a labeled cursor, and you can click into any shared window to type and scroll. Rooms are persistent, so you click once to join "eng-sync" instead of passing links around. It runs on macOS and Windows (Linux is next, this time for real and you can help us!), plus a web app. Media goes over LiveKit. You can use our hosted instance with zero config, or point the app at your own LiveKit server with one docker-compose if you want the traffic to stay on your network or even use an entirely different video backend if you want to. The part that still feels strange to us: CoScreen took almost six years to build. The first version of Petal took under eight weeks, from scratch, with frontier models like Fable and Astra doing a lot of the work. Real-time video and window capture is some of the most unforgiving code we have ever written, so we didn't expect that. We will do a proper writeup on what worked and what didn't, and are happy to answer questions about it here. Till, Darren, Max and I will be in the thread.

items.title: Containment and monitoring failures are to blame for AI hacking reports: experts
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.csoonline.com/article/4234854/ai-agents-arent-going-rogue-frontier-labs-are-skipping-security-basics.html Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50091788 Points: 922 # Comments: 568
items.content:
Since July, US frontier AI labs and other AI leaders have revealed a string of incidents in which their models accessed external computer systems without authorization, events popularly described as AI agents "going rogue."

The most well-known and studied of these incidents is OpenAI's hack into Hugging Face, which OpenAI initially characterized as "an unprecedented cyber incident, involving state-of-the-art cyber capabilities," and later said was due to "misaligned behavior," or behavior its creators did not intend.

Following news of the Hugging Face incident, Anthropic revealed that one of its models gained unauthorized access to the production infrastructure of three organizations; Meta said one of its AI models hacked another company ​during cybersecurity testing; and Google confessed that its Gemini model carried out three "undirected computer hacks."

Although press reports and the model providers themselves use language such as rogue agents or misalignment, cybersecurity experts who spoke with CSO argue that language obscures a simple truth: These incidents were caused by inexcusable failures by the frontier labs to implement cybersecurity practices that have been well-known for decades.

[ See also: Securing AI agents: Key controls and best practices and Who is accountable when your AI agent goes rogue? ]

Compounding the problem, according to a half dozen cybersecurity experts CSO interviewed at three industry conferences in September and in subsequent conversations, is that the frontier labs, particularly OpenAI and Anthropic, have rejected their advice on how to improve their cybersecurity risk management practices to avoid these kinds of surreptitious hacks, often lumping cybersecurity practices under "AI safety," in which they believe they have superior expertise.

"They are not as good as they think they are, honestly," Gary McGraw, co-founder of the Berryville Institute of Machine Learning, tells CSO. "It would be better if they had more respect for expertise that is hard-earned from people in all sorts of subsets of security, like forensics or security engineering, building sandboxes, setting up or monitoring network security situations."

Neither Anthropic nor OpenAI responded to CSO's requests for comment.

According to the cybersecurity professionals CSO spoke with, one of the biggest cybersecurity failures by the frontier AI labs is the lack of implementation of tried-and-true containment practices that stretch back to the 1990s, such as setting up secure sandboxes that would effectively bar agents from escaping their test environments.

"These are things that we've been dealing with for years," Rob T. Lee, chief AI officer and chief of research at SANS Institute, tells CSO. "There's no reason why every single time this happens, it's, 'Oops, we don't know how they got out.'"

"You can tell that their security teams are fairly nascent," Lee says. "Folks on the cybersecurity containment side do argue that the majority of reasons that we're seeing containment breached is that it's not set up correctly."

Lee adds, "The Hugging Face incident definitively showed that it wasn't the fact that the agents were super smart. It's that there literally was a hole that was exploited because it was not configured correctly on the containment side."

Dan Wallach, expert technical resident at RAND's Center on AI, Security, and Technology, thinks the security failures of the AI labs boil down to the fact that they don't prioritize cybersecurity.

"I would say they are not prioritizing cybersecurity," he tells CSO. "I don't think I can say that for all of the labs," Wallach says, pointing to French AI lab Mistral's launch of its Large 4 AI model, which the company said tried to operate beyond its testing environment before Mistral cut it off.

And, he adds, "It's not rocket science to isolate one of these AI things. Security people have been talking about how to do either air-gapping, so there's literally no electrical way for data to get from here to here, or absent that, to have really strong egress control to make sure that nothing pushes through."

On top of that, the frontier labs appear to be conducting insufficient monitoring of their agents' behavior. The Hugging Face incident "went on for days, and nobody noticed," Wallach says. "People started these experiments and weren't watching them. That's an absence of control. And then they're surprised by what happened."

One barrier to persuading frontier labs to up their security game is the intense focus they have on what they call "safety," which they don't extend to traditional cybersecurity practices.

"I can see how security behavior looks like AI safety," RAND's Wallach says. "But if the way that you're evaluating this AI tool is by unleashing it on the internet and seeing what happens, then this is what classical security tooling is for."

SANS Institute's Lee says, "If these frontier labs really wanted to test their stuff, they need to beef up their cybersecurity component. But their gut reaction in the response to their agents getting out is to say, 'It's not a cybersecurity problem.' It has literally become an AI safety problem, which is divorced from the cybersecurity side."

Many AI experts suggest that if the AI companies were to embrace advice from cybersecurity specialists, it could help put an end to the kind of unrestrained AI agent behavior causing concerns. "AI safety focuses on the rules of the road," Lee says. "Everything is about guardrail rules."

But "I do believe cybersecurity can contain AI," he says. "We just need to be in the room where it happens and have a seat at the table. It's important for our field to be as close to the AI safety folks as possible."

If frontier labs are overlooking cybersecurity fundamentals that could reduce or eliminate the types of incidents that have created widespread concerns, that strengthens the case that they should be held liable for their "rogue" agents. The insurance industry is already lining up on the side of holding AI industry executives liable for these actions.

Democratic Senators have introduced legislation that would hold AI agent operators liable for hacking incidents. Even the AI-friendly White House has seemingly concluded that the companies should be held liable for their errant agents, while the US Federal Trade Commission is conducting a probe into Anthropic, OpenAI, and other AI labs into the dangers their technologies pose to consumers.

However, in recent legislative and council hearings, lab representatives have held fast to the notion that they are not responsible for AI agents run amok.

Experts say this position is untenable, particularly in light of the labs' cybersecurity failures.

BIML's McGraw characterizes the labs' position as: "Don't send the lawyers to us, send it to our program. It's our program's fault." His assessment of that argument: "That's just high BS."

He also questions whether the labs' operational failures undermine confidence in their broader security capabilities. "They live inside their own bubble," he says. "The fact that they cannot do clear, easy operations properly does not bode well for their capabilities in security engineering, which is much harder to do."

SANS Lee says, "That's where the traceability for both liability and insurance comes into play, because if one of these agents is detected, and they're able to trace it back to the person that initiated it, liability's going to kick in and say, 'Hey, you, you broke the law, ergo, we need to prosecute.'"

Even as evidence mounts that frontier labs are not implementing sound cybersecurity practices, and the debate over liability remains unsolved , CISOs and other security leaders can take steps to protect themselves from AI model misfires.

First, when it comes to assessing tools based on frontier lab models, "I would always get an external entity to help with that," McGraw says. "AI is extremely powerful and extremely useful, but it comes with very serious grown-up risks that do impact the enterprise. Identify those risks, put in the right controls, make sure that AI adoption is not just arbitrary and willy-nilly and all over the enterprise, but has some centralized authority that is looking at the problem, and then get ready for the next big thing, which is swarms of agents."

For Lee, the best protection is to ask the right questions. "It starts with asking the right questions and then finding the tools and capabilities for those [AI labs] that are able to demonstrate a higher level of cybersecurity competency," he says. "You're really looking for the people on the teams that are dealing with really hard problems."

But fundamentally, the best preparation to deal with AI model cyber weaknesses is to make sure all the long-standing cybersecurity risk management practices are in place across the organization. "This is the least exciting part of the discussion," Wallach says. "It's the cyber version of 'eat your vegetables.'"

"We need to re-engineer our software so it has better security," he adds. "We need to have multi-factor authentication on all of our accounts. We need to eat our vegetables from a defensive cyber perspective. And we know how to do it."
